decisions.reason: As a flagship harvesting crate for a niche agricultural segment, its value is still unfolding through seasonal pooling adoption, and carrying an existing tooled product costs little, so the option is worth keeping.
Foldable large containers are a core, growing returnable-packaging category with a multi-model line and steady presentation on its own page, so there is no sign the option has failed.
Stackable crate lines are staple products with low carrying cost once moulds exist, and they serve broad food and retail demand.
Rackable pallets fit established industrial demand, and the multi-model line remains visible, so keeping it costs little relative to its option value.
Its move from its own page to a mere mention hints at weaker emphasis, but it is a low-cost niche line in a portfolio with many other options, so modest drop risk is warranted without clear failure.
It is a single-model specialty pallet whose prominence declined, which raises the drop risk, but the evidence that its value has failed is not yet conclusive.
